messages:
jlee: Heads-up — after landing the INT8 kernel selector change on the staging cluster, we're seeing decode throughput drop ~20% for long-context workloads. Prefill seems fine but decode latency spikes once KV cache hits grow.

maria: Can you paste the perf profile? Also which model and quant config? FP8/INT8/4-bit mix?

jlee: Model: redwood-13b-compat, quant: per-channel INT8 for matmuls, some layers FP16 fallback. This is with TTFT batching on (target_latency_ms=60). Profile:

```
perf_summary:
  prefill_tokens/s: 4200
  decode_tokens/s: 3300  <-- expected ~4100
  avg_decode_p99_ms: 78
  kv_cache_mem: +1.8GB on long contexts
  top_time_consumers:
    - attention_kv_pack: 34%
    - int8_dequant: 18%
    - matmul_int8: 22%
    - kernel_dispatch: 10%
```

jlee: The interesting bit is attention_kv_pack and int8_dequant. On prefill decode ratio looks weird: prefill is faster than decode by a lot.

kevin: That smells like a per-step kernel selection overhead. If the runtime is switching kernels between prefill (batched) and decode (single-step) we can hit dispatch/format cost. Any trace of kernel recompile/rebind?

perf-bot: [trace] kernel_bind_events: {104 entries, avg_bind_time_ms: 1.9, max_bind_time_ms: 6.1} 

maria: 1.9ms avg bind is high when you do many small decode steps. With TTFT we prioritize tail latency so we break batches; TPS suffers but tail latency stays low. However quantized dequant + KV packing has more memory ops.

sara: Two quick hypotheses: (1) prefill uses large contiguous matmul which hits INT8 fast-paths and streaming cache, (2) decode uses small GEMMs triggering a slower INT8 fallback and extra dequant. Also kv layout might be causing unaligned memcpy.

jlee: I ran a repro where I forced INT8->FP16 convert before the attention pack (adds 0.6ms per step) and decode throughput returned close to expected. So conversion reduces repeated dequant overhead but adds CPU/GPU ops.

kevin: Hmm. Could be calibration noise: per-channel scales chosen for prefill distribution may not match decode token distribution => runtime chooses different kernel (high-precision fallback) to avoid accuracy loss. Did the selector log which kernel was chosen per-layer?

jlee: Yes, selector logs show layer 10/11/12 choosing fallback matmul_fp16 for decode. Prefill chose matmul_int8 for the same layers.

maria: That's interesting — calibration thresholds were computed on short-context prompt sets. With long contexts, activation magnitudes shift, which invalidates some INT8 ranges causing fallback. We should run calibration on long-context traces.

sara: Agreed. Also consider caching kernel decisions by (model, layer, sequence_len_bucket) so we don't re-evaluate every step. It can reduce kernel_dispatch churn.

kevin: For batching heuristics: TTFT means we build tiny batches to keep latency low. That also increases kernel_bind frequency. Maybe switch to hybrid: use TTFT for P50 and a small windowed batching for P99 to let kernels amortize. We can tune target_latency_ms to trade TPS vs TTFT.

jlee: Quick experiment: toggled to TPS-optimized mode (larger batching) on a canary, decode tokens/s recovered to 3950 and avg_decode_p99_ms increased to 95ms but P50 stayed under 35ms. So tradeoff is visible.

perf-bot: [metric] canary_epoch_1: prefill_tokens/s=4250, decode_tokens/s=3950, avg_decode_p99_ms=95

maria: We need to decide what's the default for dedicated customers. Many prefer predictable TPS over strict TTFT. For hosted low-latency tiers keep TTFT. For dedicated default to TPS mode unless SLA requests otherwise.

kevin: Action items:
- run long-context calibration job (collect activations >32k context) — @maria
- add per-sequence_len_bucket kernel decision cache — @sara
- add short-circuit path: convert INT8->FP16 KV packing ahead of decode when fallback patterns detected — @jlee
- retro: measure memory copy alignment for KV pack -> see if we can shave 0.5ms — @infra-bot to run microbench

infra-bot: scheduled task: kv_pack_alignment_microbench queued (job id: 2026-0891). ETA 2h.

jlee: Also logging: we'll add the kernel_choice tag to traces so we can filter regressed requests. Will push a small patch to selector logs.

maria: One more note: calibrating on long-context might widen quant ranges and reduce accuracy slightly on short prompts. We should run our eval suites to check regressions. Start with 5% prompts from existing eval corpus.

kevin: Good. If the eval delta is within guardrail, promote long-context calibration. If not, consider hybrid per-prefix calibration.

sara: I'll prototype the kernel cache this afternoon. If that lowers bind_time avg below 0.5ms we may not need to change default TTFT heuristics.

jlee: Thanks team. I'll collect traces and post an update in ~3h. For now rolling back the selector change on staging to avoid noisy alerts. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — on it.

kevin: Keep me posted.

perf-bot: [note] rolling_log: selector_change reverted on staging at 1760851400.
